techStack: React 19, ReactDOM 19 — createPortal API stable, useLayoutEffect and useEffect both available
TypeScript 5.7 — NOT in strict mode; noUnusedLocals: true (every declared ref/variable must be used)
Vitest 3.x + @testing-library/react 16 + jsdom 26 — test environment simulates DOM
No CSS-in-JS; className strings used for element selection (e.g. '.detail-close-btn' for querySelector)
tsconfig lib includes DOM — HTMLElement, SVGElement, Element, document.activeElement all typed correctly
No existing useLayoutEffect in the component — must be added fresh
features: ProductDetailPanel renders: .detail-backdrop (div, aria-hidden), role=dialog .detail-panel (div), .detail-close-btn (button), conditional Spinner/error/product article
Existing useEffect #1: fetches product data when productId changes — must not be touched
Existing useEffect #2: scroll lock (document.body.style.overflow) — must not be touched
isOpen derived as productId !== null (line 20) — this is the signal for all new hooks
panelRef (HTMLDivElement) already declared and attached to .detail-panel div
Test cases: panel opens on card click, close button closes, backdrop click closes, product data renders — all must continue passing
Bug placeholder block at lines 53-59 documents the four missing behaviours
architecture: ProductDetailPanel.tsx is the only file to modify (requirement 11)
Parent is ProductListPage — passes productId and onClose; no changes needed there
Portal: ReactDOM.createPortal(JSX, document.body) at line 63/134 — renders outside React tree root
Because of portal, React onKeyDown on the panel div will NOT catch keypresses when focus is elsewhere; document-level listener required for Escape
Tab trap can be handled via a document-level keydown listener (same pattern as Escape) or via onKeyDown on the panel div — document-level is safer given portal rendering
New refs needed: prevFocusRef (Element | null) to store pre-open focused element
New hooks needed: useLayoutEffect (focus-on-open + focus-restore), useEffect (Escape listener), and a tab-trap handler (useEffect on document or onKeyDown on panel div)
edgeCases: prevFocusRef.current may be null on first render — guard with instanceof check before calling .focus()
document.activeElement returns Element | null — need 'instanceof HTMLElement || instanceof SVGElement' guard before .focus()
Element captured in prevFocusRef may be removed from DOM by close time — instanceof guard is sufficient; .focus() on a detached element is a safe no-op
Panel has only ONE focusable element (close button) during loading — Tab must wrap to itself; Shift+Tab must also wrap to itself
Panel may have ZERO focusable elements if querySelectorAll returns empty NodeList — tab-trap handler must guard against empty list (early return)
FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR must be defined as a constant (not inline) to satisfy noUnusedLocals and for reuse in the trap handler
Escape listener cleanup: useEffect cleanup function must remove the same listener reference — store handler in a const inside useEffect before addEventListener
useLayoutEffect (not useEffect) required for focus-on-open so focus moves before paint, avoiding visible flash
When isOpen goes false (close), focus restore happens in the same useLayoutEffect cleanup/else branch — must check prevFocusRef.current instanceof HTMLElement before .focus()

tasks.requirement: Requirements 1, 2, 3 — focus-on-open, capture previous focus, restore focus on close
tasks.description: Add prevFocusRef = useRef<Element | null>(null). Add a useLayoutEffect that depends on [isOpen]: when isOpen is true, assign document.activeElement to prevFocusRef.current, then call .focus() on panelRef.current?.querySelector('.detail-close-btn'); when isOpen is false, call .focus() on prevFocusRef.current if it instanceof HTMLElement or SVGElement.

tasks.requirement: Requirements 4, 5 — document-level Escape keydown listener with cleanup
tasks.description: Add a useEffect that depends on [isOpen, onClose]: when isOpen is true, define a handler const that checks event.key === 'Escape' and calls onClose(), attach it via document.addEventListener('keydown', handler), and return a cleanup that calls document.removeEventListener('keydown', handler). When isOpen is false, register no listener (or guard with early return).

tasks.requirement: Requirement 6 — Tab/Shift+Tab focus trap cycling within the panel
tasks.description: Define a FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR constant: 'button:not([disabled]), a[href], input:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])'. Add a useEffect that depends on [isOpen]: when isOpen is true, define a trap handler that on keydown Tab/Shift+Tab calls event.preventDefault(), queries panelRef.current?.querySelectorAll(FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR), and wraps focus (Tab on last → first; Shift+Tab on first → last). If the NodeList is empty, return early. Attach via document.addEventListener('keydown', trapHandler) with cleanup via removeEventListener.
